page: Microsoft Azure L96s_v4 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the Lsv4 family, virtualized via Microsoft Hyper-V. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs derived from 48 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz with a 260 MB L3 cache. The hardware configuration includes 768.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB per core, and a substantial local storage capacity of 23038 GB. No GPUs are present on this instance, and it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core capabilities, with Geekbench multi-core scores and static web serving throughput reaching the top 10% tier. Stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Passmark CPU scores fall within the top 25% tier. Single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core results in the middle 50% tier, though Geekbench single-core scores remain in the top 25%. Memory subsystem performance is robust, showing top 25% tier results for both cached small-block read bandwidth at 6198.6 GB/sec and uncached large-block read/write bandwidth.

With its massive 23 TB local storage capacity and 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this server provides high resource density for data-intensive operations. It is optimized for large-scale databases, high-throughput web serving, and memory-intensive workloads. The inclusion of Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions supports CPU-based AI workloads, reflected in strong prompt processing speeds for medium and large LLM models, though text generation speeds for large 70B models remain average. The high density of storage and memory relative to the vCPU count offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring massive local scratch space or large in-memory datasets without needing external storage attachments.
description: Microsoft Azure L96s_v4 is an x86_64 server in the Lsv4 family, powered by a 96-vCPU Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz with 260 MB of L3 cache. It features 768.0 GB of RAM and 23038 GB of local storage, with no integrated GPUs. Benchmarks show top 10% tier performance in multi-core Geekbench tests, image processing, and static web serving throughput, alongside top 25% tier memory bandwidth. While single-core CPU performance sits in the middle 50% tier, its multi-threaded capabilities and massive local storage capacity make it highly efficient for large-scale databases, Redis deployments, and memory-intensive enterprise applications. The hardware supports advanced vector and matrix extensions, enabling efficient local data processing and medium-scale LLM inference without requiring dedicated GPU hardware.
